paragraphs: A recorder of boys who know what they love and pursue it with passion.
In his room hangs a note: “Make today happier than yesterday.” To me, he seems to know how to live in the present.

Looking at him, I sometimes feel the regrets of my own past—I should have traveled more, studied more languages. Seeing something burning in him, I turn that regret into a resolve to focus more fully on now. Then—even now!

He is one of the dear friends who make me feel so much. In 2026 he has taken up the camera. He has become a colleague. In his photographs I see the present being held. And I cheer him on—him, and myself.
